national_raw_news.title: India, China agree to discuss ways to improve understanding of LAC for better border management: MEA
national_raw_news.content: The Ministry of External Affairs today said that India and China continue to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the Line of Actual Control. Replying to media queries on recent comments by DG ITBP in New Delhi this evening, Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the situation in the India-China border areas gets disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns. He added that the two sides have also agreed to discuss ways to improve understanding of LAC in appropriate areas for better border management. Mr Jaiswal emphasised that the maintenance of peace and tranquillity in the border areas is essential for the overall development of bilateral relations. On claims that Iranian aircraft were denied airspace clearance, Mr Jaiswal said New Delhi continues to facilitate transport of life saving medicines to Iran. He remarked that the ongoing conflict in the region have posed new challenges to the flight connectivity between the two countries. He underlined that India continues to be in communication with Iranian counterparts to facilitate transportation of life saving medicines as a humanitarian gesture. Replying to a query on the fourteen Indian nationals involved in yacht incident off Yemen coast, Mr Jaiswal said Ministry has been in touch with parties there and all these Indian nationals are safe in Hodeidah. He said the Ministry remains committed to the safety and security of Indian nationals abroad. On Indians stuck in Saudi Arabia, the spokesperson said that around 3000 stranded Umrah pilgrims have traveled back home on available flights. He said that in addition to this, more than ten thousand normal Umrah pilgrims who were booked on available flights have also returned. He informed arrangements are under discussion to facilitate the return of other Umrah pilgrims at the earliest. Mr Jaiswal said Indian Embassy and Consulate in Saudi Arabia are also in touch with people who are stuck there and are rendering all possible support. On India’s defence exports, Mr Jaiswal underlined that all defence exports are in keeping with national obligations and laws and guidelines.

national_raw_news.title: Chhattisgarh freed from Naxalism with combined efforts of central & state govts: President M...
national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu has said that Chhattisgarh was freed from the menace of Naxalism with the combined efforts of central and state governments, and it is now on the path of progress by moving away from the path of Naxalism. Addressing the ‘Bastar Dussehra Festival 2026’ event at Lalbag Maidan in Jagdalpur, she also expressed confidence that youth tribal communities would actively participate in the country’s journey towards becoming a developed nation. The President lauded the efforts to provide financial facilities to tribal entrepreneurs and connect them with markets. She said, these efforts would help achieve the goal of building a developed India by 2047 through equitable development. The President urged people to protect the forests and hills of their region, emphasising that these natural resources provide food, water and other essentials for life. She said that protecting nature should be the primary responsibility of every community. The President said that the Bastar Dussehra festival brings together tribal communities from across the region. She also described the traditional Muria Darbar as a reflection of democratic values, where people present their concerns and grievances to their leaders. The President is on a two-day visit to Chhattisgarh. During her visit to Lalbagh Maidan, the President visited various stalls showcasing the Bastar Dussehra festival and interacted with local school children. The programme was also addressed by Chhattisgarh Governor Ramen Deka and Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai. Several other ministers were also present on the occasion. Earlier in the day, the President visited the Maa Danteshwari Temple in Jagdalpur and offered prayers according to traditional rituals. Later, she attended the traditional Muria Darbar at Sirhasar Bhavan, a significant event associated with the world-famous Bastar Dussehra festival. During the interaction, the President met local tribal leaders, priests and traditional community representatives, including Manjhis and Chalkis, and listened to their concerns.

national_raw_news.title: India Counters Pakistan’s Claims on Religious Freedom at UN
national_raw_news.content: India has criticised Pakistan at the United Nations, recalling its refusal to acknowledge the bodies of its soldiers killed during the 1999 Kargil War, while raising concerns over its remarks on religious freedom and burial rights. First Secretary at India’s Permanent Mission to the UN, Bhavika Mangalanandan, said the Indian Army had buried several Pakistani soldiers with military honours and in accordance with Islamic rites. Her remarks came during a discussion on an interim report by UN Special Rapporteur on freedom of religion and belief, Nazila Ghanea, which raised concerns over alleged denial of funeral rights in Jammu and Kashmir. Mangalanandan also criticised Pakistan over the treatment of minorities, saying their numbers were declining and their rights were regularly abused. She said a country unable to ensure the safety of its own minorities had no standing to lecture India, and urged Pakistan to focus on developments in areas of Jammu and Kashmir under its illegal occupation, including Rawalakot. She further questioned the report’s approach to the burial rights of terrorists, arguing that the rights of victims of terrorism also deserved due consideration. She also accused the report of selectively highlighting human rights concerns while overlooking similar incidents in other regions, including the developed world.

national_raw_news.title: Mona Agarwal’s World Record Highlights India’s Medal Haul 5 hours ago 78
national_raw_news.content: At the Asian Para Games, India continued its medal-winning run, taking its overall tally to 104 medals, including 27 gold, 34 silver and 43 bronze. In shooting, Mona Agarwal clinched gold in the women’s 50-metre rifle three positions SH1 event, setting a new world record with a score of 357.5 to claim her second gold medal of the Games. In para-athletics, Sandeep Kumar shattered the T44 world record with a time of 52.28 seconds to win gold in the men’s 400 metres, while Ajay Kumar secured bronze in the same event. Haney also struck gold in the men’s javelin throw F37 event with a world-record effort of 60.49 metres. In para-archery, Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi won gold in the men’s recurve doubles event. In para-badminton, Nitesh Kumar clinched gold in the men’s singles SL3 event, while Naveen Sivakumar won gold in the men’s singles SL4 category. India also secured six silver medals across para-athletics, para-archery and para-badminton. Parmod won silver in the men’s 1,500-metre T46 event, while Pramod Bhagat finished second in the men’s singles SL3 final. Bhawna and Pooja claimed silver in women’s recurve doubles, and Nimisha Chakkungalparambil won silver in the women’s long jump T47 event with a best effort of 5.37 metres. In para-badminton, Nithya Sre Sivan won silver in women’s singles SH6, while Thulasimathi Murugesan secured silver in the women’s singles SU5 event. Thulasimathi Murugesan and Nitesh Kumar also clinched silver in the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 event, losing to Indonesia’s Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramdani in the final. India also added a bronze medal in men’s doubles MD4 table tennis through Jehan Dorab Madan and Shubham Wadhwa.

national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that the youth have always remained at the centre of his government’s policies and initiatives. Inaugurating the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi today, Mr Modi said that for the past 25 years, he has been serving the nation to the best of his ability as head of the government. Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the government has introduced the National Education Policy to align the country’s education system with the needs of a New India. He added that the policy emphasises India’s rich traditions and knowledge, imparting education in mother tongue, modern science and emerging technologies. Prime Minister Modi said that all institutions must work towards the common goals of national development and scaling the country’s pride. He stressed the need to unite society against divisive forces, promote self-reliance and involve every citizen in the resolve to build a developed India by 2047. Prime Minister said that India has brought back more than 650 stolen ancient idols and antiquities from abroad over the past twelve years. He said that the country’s cultural heritage is being restored and its cultural sites are gaining global recognition. Mr Modi highlighted that India’s cultural sites are increasingly becoming part of UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Akashvani Correspondent reports that the three-day Sammelan has brought together over nine thousand participants from India and abroad. It marks the culmination of the year-long celebrations commemorating 75 years of the Chinmaya Mission, a global spiritual movement founded by Swami Chinmayananda in 1951. The year-long celebrations began last year with the Prime Minister releasing a Tamil versification of the Bhagavad Gita. Over the decades, the Mission has expanded its work across spiritual education, cultural preservation, youth empowerment and community service.

national_raw_news.title: Satellite-Tagged Amur Falcons Return to Manipur After Migrating Across 23 Countries 1 hour ago 43
national_raw_news.content: The two satellite-tagged Amur Falcons, Apapang and Alang, have returned to Manipur after travelling across 23 countries in Asia and Africa, marking the successful completion of their nearly year-long tracking journey. In a social media post, Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav said that the birds arrived in Manipur yesterday, 11 days after departing from their breeding grounds in northeastern China. He noted that the two falcons were tagged by scientists of the Wildlife Institute of India in November 2025. Akashvani Correspondent reports that the return of the Amur falcons marks the completion of a round-trip migration journey, highlighting the remarkable long-distance movements of the migratory birds. The falcons are now expected to spend two to three weeks at select stopover sites in the mountainous areas of Tamenglong district in Manipur. During this period, they will feed on termites and build up essential fat reserves for their next migratory leg. From Manipur, the birds are expected to undertake a six-day non-stop flight of nearly six thousand kilometres to Somalia, including a challenging three thousand kilometre crossing of the Arabian Sea. The annual arrival of the Amur Falcons is eagerly awaited by local communities in Manipur, who have played a significant role in protecting the migratory birds.

national_raw_news.title: CAQM reviews paddy stubble management measures in Ropar, Hoshiyarpur and Amritsar
national_raw_news.content: CAQM reviews paddy stubble management measures in Ropar, Hoshiyarpur and Amritsar Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर CAQM reviews paddy stubble management measures in Ropar, Hoshiyarpur and Amritsar ANI | Updated: Oct 23, 2026 20:54 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Amritsar (Punjab) [India], October 23 (ANI): A high-level team led by the Chairperson, Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM), visited thermal power and CBG plants, Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK), farm fields and a biomass plant in Ropar, Hoshiyarpur and Amritsar in the State of Punjab. The team reviewed the preparedness and took stock of various in-situ and ex-situ measures being implemented on the ground for effective paddy straw management and prevention of stubble burning incidents during the ongoing paddy harvesting season, according to the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. CAQM directed the State authorities to achieve co-firing targets in thermal power plants with special focus on ensuring compliance with emission norms. During the visit to KVK, the team saw a demonstration of machinery for in-situ and ex-situ use. The team also assessed the adequacy and availability of machinery to facilitate farmers in managing paddy residue. In addition, the team reviewed the arrangements and mechanisms in place for the maximum utilisation of paddy straw in thermal power plants and biomass plants utilising paddy stubble as part of ex-situ management. With paddy harvesting gaining momentum, the Commission emphasised the need for intensified and concerted efforts by all concerned authorities to ensure that farmers have adequate access to CRM Machinery on time. The Commission directed that facilitation of farmers be maximised, with particular focus on ensuring the availability and effective deployment of machinery in accordance with the emerging requirements during the peak harvesting period. The Commission directed State Authorities to strengthen these ecosystems for paddy stubble management to minimise stubble burning incidents. The need for proactive field-level monitoring and timely resolution of operational gaps was also emphasised to ensure effective implementation of the ongoing paddy straw management interventions. With growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and generative AI applications driving demand for high-performance data centres, India's data centre capacity has grown rapidly from 375 MW in CY20 to 1,575 MW in CY26. Capacity is further projected to reach 8,000 MW by CY30, highlighting the sector's robust growth outlook. The data centre capacity pipeline growth is driven by increasing demand from cloud services, AI workloads, and digital transformation initiatives, as investments by hyperscalers and data centre operators continue to strengthen India's position as a key data centre market in the Asia-Pacific region. Source: Industry Reports, PIB, CareEdge Research (Note: 2026 data is as of August 2026, P stands for projections) Further, investment in India’s data centre sector is projected to increase from ₹0.36 trillion in FY26 to ₹1.31 trillion by FY32, reflecting its growing importance in India's digital infrastructure ecosystem, with a 20-year tax horizon extending to 2047. Accelerating Cost Efficiency Remains Key Concern As the Digital India infrastructure adds another disruptor to its plan: mega Data Centres across the national landscape, making technology sustainable and cost-effective, command the long game. The demand for power to run these current and projected facilities, and for water to cool the heat produced by data centres, currently makes headlines as economies weigh cooling technologies, cost-effectiveness, and future outlook regarding optimal usability of AI. The expected electricity demand from the growth of AI and other large-scale data centres, as per the Ministry of Power, is estimated to reach 17 GW by 2031–32, with the current capacity being about 1575 MW. However, water requirements for cooling data centres of this scale are subject to the capacity of data centres and the cooling system technology. In this regard, as per International Energy Agency (IEA) estimates, individual hyperscale data centres with a 100MW facility could require 2.5 billion litres of water annually, equivalent to the needs of approximately 80,000 people. Thus, freshwater dependence and the volume of water used under various cooling technologies become the key to making data centres cost-efficient for the future. Moreover, as cooling choice drives both power and water consumption, traditional systems like HVAC and chiller-based air-cooling systems are increasingly replaced by more efficient and relatively lower-cost alternatives such as direct-to-chip liquid cooling, adiabatic cooling, and immersion cooling. national_raw_news.content: C-DAC, Bank Of India Join Hands To Develop Indigenous Quantum Technologies For Banking Tech C-DAC, Bank Of India Join Hands To Develop Indigenous Quantum Technologies For Banking Swarajya Staff Oct 23, 2026 | Updated 04:35 PM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Pic Via PIB The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) and public sector lender Bank of India (BOI) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to jointly explore indigenous quantum technologies and other advanced computing applications for the banking sector. According to a Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology release issued on Friday (23 October), the agreement was signed on 22 October and covers joint research, technology demonstrations, pilot projects and capacity-building initiatives. A key objective of the partnership is to develop a Quantum Ecosystem for Financial Innovation, focusing on technologies that could strengthen cybersecurity, operational resilience and decision-making in banking. The two organisations will explore quantum-inspired and quantum-safe technologies, identify potential banking applications and develop proofs of concept in secure testing environments before evaluating their feasibility for wider adoption. The collaboration will combine C-DAC's expertise in quantum computing, high-performance computing, artificial intelligence, blockchain and cybersecurity with Bank of India's banking operations and technology infrastructure. Beyond quantum technologies, the agreement also covers applications such as AI-driven fraud detection, credit and financial analytics, intelligent document processing, smart contracts, digital identity and secure data sharing. The partnership will additionally support training programmes in quantum computing, quantum security, artificial intelligence and blockchain to develop specialised technical capabilities within the financial sector. national_raw_news.content: India Steps Up Indigenous Telecom Research As C-DOT Establishes 6G, AI Centre At IIT BHU Tech India Steps Up Indigenous Telecom Research As C-DOT Establishes 6G, AI Centre At IIT BHU Swarajya Staff Oct 23, 2026 | Updated 03:34 PM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Pic Via PIB The Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT), the telecom research and development arm of the Department of Telecommunications, has established its sixth Centre of Excellence (CoE) at the Indian Institute of Technology (BHU), Varanasi, to advance research in next-generation communication technologies. According to a Ministry of Communications release issued on Friday (23 October), C-DOT and IIT BHU signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to facilitate collaborative research, technology development and capacity building in emerging telecommunications technologies. The centre will focus on 5G Advanced and 6G technologies , artificial intelligence-driven communication systems, quantum and post-quantum communications, cybersecurity and advanced wireless networks. Research areas will also include very large-scale Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems, integrated sensing and communication, and AI-native communication networks and devices. The collaboration aims to connect academic research with practical telecommunications requirements by bringing together researchers, faculty members, students and C-DOT technology experts. The MoU was signed in the presence of C-DOT Executive Vice President Pankaj Kumar Dalela and IIT BHU Director Professor Amit Patra. The signing ceremony was followed by the inauguration of the centre. The establishment of the CoE further expands C-DOT’s national network of Centres of Excellence to six, building on its existing collaborations with IIT Kanpur, IIT Gandhinagar, IIT Roorkee, IIT Hyderabad and IISc Bengaluru through FSID. The centres are intended to support indigenous technology development, specialised research and talent creation in India's telecommunications sector. national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation Towards Future-Ready Data Leaders: Comprehensive Capacity Building recommendations by Committee in MoSPI Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 11:03PM by PIB Delhi The chairman of the Committee for Reforming Capacity Building of the Indian Statistical Service (ISS), Sh. P. R. Meshram, Director General (Data Governance), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) submitted the Committee's report to Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI. This marks an important milestone toward strengthening the capacity-building framework for ISS officers. The Committee comprised senior MoSPI officers, knowledge partners, and industry experts. The Committee reviewed existing ISS training programmes, identified emerging capacity building requirements, and recommended future-oriented training aligned with the Competency Based Capacity Building (CBCB) framework of Mission Karmayogi . The framework reflects the evolving role of ISS officers in data governance, advanced analytics, emerging technologies, and evidence-based policymaking, in alignment with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047. The report has been prepared through a consultative and evidence-based approach, drawing on the Statistical Training Needs Assessment, existing ISS training programmes, Mission Karmayogi frameworks, international best practices, Committee deliberations, and stakeholder consultations. The Report presents a future oriented capacity building roadmap comprising three interconnected components. The System of Today , which reviews the existing ISS training ecosystem, capability area practices, and institutional arrangements at National Statistical Systems Training Academy (NSSTA) . The System of Tomorrow , which establishes a role linked, competency based capacity-building framework covering seven priority capability pillars; and Strategic Recommendations giving actionable measures to transition from current to the envisioned future system to strengthening ISS training, develop future ready competencies, and enhance NSSTA's institutional capacity. The report outlines an integrated framework comprising the ISS training ecosystem, capability pillars, and institutional architecture. It defines role expectations and assesses the competencies required for each role across functional, domain, and behavioral domains. The framework is to be anchored in the National Statistical Systems Training Academy (NSSTA) , with an emphasis on strengthening human resources, training delivery, and governance to effectively implement training reforms. Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI, complimented the Committee and the NSSTA team for their efforts and comprehensive, forward-looking recommendations. He reaffirmed the commitment to strengthening NSSTA as a pivotal training anchor for Indian Statistical Systems. national_raw_news.content: Drinking Water and Sanitation Department organises virtual conference as follow up to Water Summit Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Drinking Water and Sanitation Department organises virtual conference as follow up to Water Summit ANI | Updated: Oct 22, 2026 19:45 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, on Thursday organised the fourth virtual conference with States and Union Territories as part of a series of thematic consultations being held in follow-up to the Departmental Summit on Water 2026 held on September 1 and 2. The conference focused on strengthening convergence between Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 and the 16th Finance Commission to advance source sustainability, water security and Gram Panchayat-led planning for sustainable rural drinking water service delivery. The virtual conference brought together senior officials from State PHEDs/Rural Water Supply Departments, Panchayati Raj Departments and representatives from the Ministries of Panchayati Raj, Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India and National Informatics Centre. State rural water supply departments, including Karnataka, Odisha and Madhya Pradesh, shared best practices and field experiences on leveraging Finance Commission grants for strengthening rural water supply systems, improving O&M arrangements, enhancing community participation and strengthening local governance mechanisms. Addressing the conference, Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS, stated that with the extension of JJM 2.0, the focus now shifts from infrastructure creation to ensuring functionality, sustainability and quality service delivery. He emphasised that the true measure of success lies not merely in asset creation but in ensuring that rural households continue to receive reliable and safe drinking water through well-maintained and financially sustainable systems. Meena underlined the pivotal role of Gram Panchayats in rural water governance and noted that the 73rd Constitutional Amendment places drinking water and sanitation among the key responsibilities of local self-governments. He stressed that Gram Panchayats must take leadership in preparing comprehensive annual O&M plans, mobilising local resources, managing service delivery and ensuring accountability for water supply infrastructure created under JJM and other programmes. Referring to the 16th Finance Commission framework, he highlighted that tied grants provide a significant opportunity to strengthen the sustainability of drinking water and sanitation services at the grassroots level. He noted that of the total Rural Local Body (RLB) grants recommended by the 16th Finance Commission, a substantial share has been earmarked for water and sanitation-related activities. He emphasised that these grants should be utilised primarily for operation and maintenance, source sustainability, water quality management, service delivery improvements and strengthening local institutional capacity rather than creation of new infrastructure where existing assets require maintenance and support. The Secretary focused on three key pillars of sustainable financing for rural water supply systems such as effective utilisation of Finance Commission grants, ii. convergence with other available programmes, and iii. schemes, and progressive strengthening of user-charge collection mechanisms.
